text1: Fast, cheap, and out of control; Magellan interceptor pilots swear by the pivoting gunpod in a dogfight, but their greatest asset is their disposability.
Fast, cheap, and durable; these Blackcollar rebuilds of the Chela are both more survivable, and a little bit less combat-capable, than the standard model.
Fast, cheap, and easy to fly; these lightweight rebuilds of the Chela are both more forgiving, and a little bit less combat-capable, than their purely military cousins.
Fast, cheap, and out of control; Magellan interceptor pilots swear by the pivoting gunpod in a dogfight. This improved Skytiger variant mounts a heavier cannon.
Fast, cheap, and durable; these scout fighter rebuilds of the Chela are both more survivable, and a little bit less combat-capable, than their purely military cousins.

A testament to both the recklessness and the ingenuity of the Herd's engineers, the Goforth carrier is an amalgam from a variety of donor craft that manages, somehow, to be more than the sum of its parts. Heavy armor plating and hot-rodded drives make for an odd, but highly effective combination; it wouldn't pass muster in most space fleets, but then, most Herd spacers aren't spit-and-polish types, either.
Crude, slow, and armored well beyond need or reason, the Stave is a delivery system for a sawed-off Heavy Flenser, allowing it to simply chop other fighters in half with a storm of explosive slugs.
An advanced point-defense drone, designed to compliment the Almarshad gunship.
Fast and well shielded, this light fighter version of the military-grade Jitte remains formidable in close combat. Highly effective as a patrol and space-superiority fighter.
Powerful, fast and well shielded, a heavy fighter that can survive close combat around cruisers and capitals. Highly effective as a frigate-killing brawler or space-superiority fighter.

Powerful, fast and well shielded, a heavy fighter that can survive close combat around cruisers and capitals, refitted by the Blackcollars for close support. Highly effective as a generalist fighter-bomber.
Fast and well shielded, this light fighter version of the military-grade Jitte has been refitted by The Herd for a more missile-centric loadout. Highly effective as a space-superiority fighter.
Powerful, fast and well shielded, a heavy fighter that can survive close combat around cruisers and capitals, refitted as a multirole strike-fighter by the Tichel Concern.

A heavily armored bomber, deploying twin bays for electron bombs. While not the equal of other bombers in raw damage potential, it is a formidable support bomber that leaves ships crippled and ripe for followup strikes.
A heavily armored bomber, deploying twin bays for fusion bombs. Unlike the original model, the Skytiger variant does considerably more raw damage, making it a fearsome strike craft.
A heavily armored bomber, deploying twin rocket grenade bays. While not the equal of other bombers in raw armor penetration, it remains a formidable strike craft.

A tough, well-protected escort corvette, armed with a flexible turret and anti-fighter missiles. Primarily a defensive unit, intended to keep enemy fighter swarms at bay or shoot down incoming bombers and their payloads.

A tough, well-protected strike corvette, armed with a fusion lance and anti-fighter missiles. Unlike other corvette variants, it is intended to take the fight to the enemy, and can carve through the armor of larger ships with ease.

A tough, well-protected escort corvette, armed with a suite of beam weapons. Primarily a defensive unit, it is intended to keep enemy fighter swarms at bay or shoot down incoming bombers and their payloads.

A vicious and highly effective fighter drone. The combination of devastating weaponry and incredible speed makes for an extreme challenge in combat; few unaugmented Magellan pilots have tangled with a Swarmfighter wing and lived to tell the tale.

A light bomber, carrying a small bay of cluser bombs and highly effective defense systems in the form of an afterburner and an omni-shield. While not the hardest-hitting, it is a respectable fast attack craft.

Surpassingly ugly and equally effective; a battlecruiser design that foregoes all attempt at subtlety in favor of raw frontal firepower, built around a huge spinal fusion lance and backed up by an impressive array of ballistics and a single flight deck. These ships represent a new, aggressive engagement philosophy for the conservative, doctrinaire Magellan Fleet.

Nothing more than a titanic slab of armor pocked by engine nozzles and weapons emplacements, these immense and terrible gun platforms are the Magellan Fleet's raison d'etre; the enormous triphammers meant to smash an enemy's battle-line into glowing clouds of slag, gas, and shoals of twisted metal fragments.
A tried and true fleet carrier design, armed lightly but more than adequate to provide front-line fighter and missile support.

Through a remarkable feat of engineering, the Levellers have rebuilt the Hager-class supply ship into a high capacity drone carrier. While the ship itself remains lightly armed and poorly defended, the overwhelming waves of drones it can unleash at a moment's notice places it firmly in the role of an effective support ship.

Simple, durable, both well-equipped and comparatively rare, these rugged combat freighters are heavier on the 'combat' side. While not the equal of dedicated patrol ships, woe betide the pirates who find themselves between the crossed arcs of her gun turrets.
Given the paucity of meaningful, or at least high-volume, multi-system commerce in Magellan space, it's more remarkable that a ship like this exists at all than that it's so well-found. The hardy few Magellan traders who could be called 'independent' are often a short step up from pirates themselves, legitimized only by their fast talking and much-thumbed letters of marque, as well as careful timing - never hitting a ship that can't be overlooked, and always ensuring that any goods pilfered are expertly fenced, or flawlessly appear to be legitimate salvage.

A solid and unimaginative line cruiser, this veteran design is essentially unchanged from the first models rushed out to defend the Khamn system during the First AI War. What it lacks in offensive firepower, it makes up for in sheer, stubborn ability to take punishment and a ruggedness that has kept many individual hulls flying well past the century mark.
An automated defense drone, equipped with light weapons and its own drone fighter wing.
A wing of automated bomber drones, heavily armored and equipped with a high-capacity bomb bay.
A wing of automated gun drones, heavily armored and equipped with a pair of twin-linked machine guns.
A small automated defense drone, armed with a mix of light cannons.
A small automated defense drone, armed with missiles and ballistic weapons.
A heavy automated defense drone, armed with a wide variety of weapons and equipped with a Damper Field for sustained area defense.
An automated long range defense platform, armed with a single large weapon.

Unusual for a Magellan ship, this fast, mobile combatant emphasizes alpha strikes, and sports a fearsome armored prow for ramming. Captains are cautioned not to allow enemies around to the rear, as most weapons and the heaviest armor are oriented forward.

Fresh from the nanoforge with the latest improvements in Magellan technology, this Blackcollar refit of the Capella-class destroyer sports a menacing and stylish paintjob that incorporates a stealth coating, and comes equipped with an experimental neural interface, purchased at great cost from Tri-Tachyon agents.

A new, high-end frigate design, designed to shore up the general weakness of Magellan skirmishing forces. The Almarshad's most unusual feature is an advanced flak drone, which provides it with impressive point-defense capability.

A militarized Phillips-class freighter converted into a fuel tanker role. Given the insular nature of the Protectorate, the use of these ships outside of the Fleet is heavily controlled, and is limited to the few merchant captains who have secured the patronage of Magellan elites.
A lightweight drone missile, capable of loitering for extended periods and equipped with a low-powered PD maser.
An ancient design, this highly modular escort craft fits roughly into the modern 'frigate' category. It excells at nothing in particular, but requires little to no regular maintenance.

These ponderous ancient craft were reportedly the command vessels of the Fleet that lead the Magellan exiles to their present home. Their full specifications have largely been forgotten; even their class name was a chance discovery by a programmer-archaeologist. What dormant systems lurk in their cavernous internal bays, only the brave techminers who explore their depths can say. Such technology could be of great interest to the Tichel Mercantile Concern on Pariya.

These ponderous ancient craft were reportedly the command vessels of the Fleet that lead the Magellan exiles to their present home. Their full specifications have largely been forgotten; even their class name was a chance discovery by a programmer-archaeologist. What dormant systems lurk in their cavernous internal bays, only the brave techminers who explore their depths can say.

A simple and utterly disposable corvette, useful mainly as a screen for other vessels. The use of forbidden AI technology has made the Leveller movement a pariah in the Sector, and alienated many of the potential allies who could bolster their numbers - but allows the ship to be operated with a very small, or no, crew.

A simple and utterly disposable corvette, useful mainly as a screen for other vessels. The use of forbidden AI technology has made the Leveller movement a pariah in the Sector, and alienated many of the potential allies who could bolster their numbers - but allows the ship to be operated with a very small, or no, crew.

A fast light cruiser, newer than much of the Magellan Fleet but built to a well-balanced design, emphasizing long-range scouting and all-round defense. Production has increased markedly since the end of the Second AI War, and is rapidly replacing older cruiser designs in Fleet service.
A simple, stolid brick of a ship, designed for nothing so much as outright brawling at short to medium ranges. More versatile slots than a typical Domain standard design.
A tried and true Magellan frigate that has been in continuous service since the First AI War. It is somewhat undergunned for its size, but is perfectly capable in a close fight.
An entirely unimpressive light freighter, the bulk of independent Magellan commerce is carried in these durable hulls; better-protected than most, but scarcely cost-efficient.

A newer longer-ranged vessel compared to most of the Fleet's destroyers, the Kant class is equipped with a single fighter bay, top-flight sensor drones, and high-capacity fuel tanks. Lightly-built in comparison to a pure combat vessel, it is designed for long-range scouting and anti-piracy duties - at which it, predictably, excels.
Not too far divergent from the first testbed phase-cloak platforms built by the Protectorate, this ungainly, lumpen cruiser is nevertheless a highly effective design in the right hands.

A durable, tough phase frigate, notable mainly for the outsized bow mount. One unusual feature of the Yeager is the modular internal structure. Unlike typical phase ships, an enterprising captain could easily convert some of the missile storage spaces into room for extra crew.

Slow, bulky, heavily armored and largely defenseless; penal logistics crews have been a staple of Magellan Fleet doctrine for centuries, and this rugged supply ship has outlived several generations of the hapless malcontents who flew her.

A new-model combat cruiser, showing a certain amount of promise as a fleet-level support ship and artillery platform. An unusual asymmetric hull holds a monstrous missile installation, delivering heavy salvoes at long range.

Tough, swift, and armed to the teeth; a mainstay of Magellan patrol operations and an iconic standard-bearer for the Fleet. The forward quadrant of these ships is a zone of death for anything smaller than another destroyer.
Tough and versatile, a frigate design for all seasons, equipped with an afterburning propulsion pack. Ideal for close pursuits and fleet picket duty.

A light carrier overhaul of the Talley class merchanter that replaces its main cargo bay with a flight deck and missile autoloader. Hundreds of these ships were built in response to the First AI War, where they quickly proved their worth in combat. Being based on an already well regarded foundation, the design has remained popular with the Fleet ever since.

A light carrier overhaul of the Talley class merchanter that replaces its main cargo bay with a flight deck and missile autoloader. Despite being an older design, the Blackcollars favor the Ayres over newer and heavier combat carriers due to its combination of excellent mobility and capacity for short bursts of exceptional firepower.

An antiquated, temperamental design, the Musa is either an elegant, timeless classic, or a clapped-out fuel-guzzling relic, depending on who you ask, the condition of the hull, and whether they've had to clean the notoriously fickle thruster-injection filters lately. Regardless, it's a tough and well-found little cargo ship; large for a frigate, decently armed, and remarkably agile.
One of the rare civilian ships unique to Magellan space, this antiquated vessel is as well-armed as some patrol frigates in more secure regions.

The former ship of choice for patrol officers and discerning nobles alike, the Mallory-class clipper combines speed, adaptability, reactor performance, and firepower into one sleek package. However, changing priorities following the Second AI Wars saw production for the civilian market all but halted. Military procurement has also slowed in favor of the newer and far more economical Kant-class scout ship. The miniscule handful of newly built clippers are most often personally doled out by the Lord Regent as patronage rewards.
An ancient escort/interceptor fighter, for exclusive use with the Mallory clipper. High speed and generous missile storage make for an highly effective general-purpose fighter/interceptor.

An ancient heavy support fighter, for exclusive use with the Mallory clipper. While not especially fast, the Rounder is agile and well-shielded, making it exceptionally dangerous to frigates and destroyers.
An ancient heavy support fighter, for exclusive use with the Mallory clipper. This inventive Leveller conversion to a light bomber is surprisingly effective.

An expertly rebuilt Blackcollar variant of the Rounder heavy fighter, fitted with modernized systems that can be maintained from a contemporary carrier flight deck. In combat, the fighter remains close to its carrier and deploys a steady stream of long range missile fire.
A small pod for Balefire heavy fusion missiles. The strike craft sized magazine requires redock and reloading once munitions have been expended.

A launch tube for Balefire heavy fusion missiles. While not as powerful as dedicated anti-armor missiles, the Balefire is more effective against shields, and the magazine can sustain fire for a considerable time.

A launch system for Balefire heavy fusion missiles. While not as powerful as dedicated anti-armor missiles, the Balefire is more effective against shields, and this compact launcher carries generous reloads.

A launch system for Balefire heavy fusion missiles. While not as powerful as dedicated anti-armor missiles, the Balefire is more effective against shields. This capital grade launcher carries a vast internal magazine for extended engagements.
A large-caliber smoothbore cannon, firing a scattering blast of explosive shells at medium range.

A compact and terrifying fragmentation shotgun, flinging an explosive shell surrounded by a cloud of semi-molten debris that chews up damaged armor and unprotected hull. A simple target-tracking system allows it to be used as supplemental point defense.
While punishments for misuse of resources in the Fleet's lower ranks tend to the draconian and final, that doesn't stop tertiary-battery crews assigned to Bonecracker stations from setting up occasional unauthorized skeet-shooting matches, using scraps of rusted hull plating for targets. Many astute commanders look the other way; anything that improves gunnery performance can be forgiven, so long as there are no major accidents.
A clumsy but devastating heavy autocannon, firing enormous semi-molten bolts. The heavier bolts have excellent penetration, and allow even a single mount to chew through a substantial belt of armor.

Firing a burst of semi-molten flechettes with a weak electrical charge, the Bonesaw electrostatic autogun is a fearsome brawling weapon, albeit quite ineffective against shields and with lower than expected penetration against heavy armor.

Firing bursts of semi-molten bolts with a weak electrical charge, the Bonechipper electrostatic autogun is a fearsome interceptor weapon, ineffective against shields and with low penetration against heavy armor.
A twin-mount electrostatic cannon, the Boneshaker couples the reliable weapons with a high-torque traversing motor and a robust burst regulator.
A twin mounting of the Bonechipper, this turret couples the reliable weapons with a high-torque traversing motor and a robust burst regulator.
A triple-mounted electrostatic cannon, favored by captains who need a little extra edge. While tracking suffers from the heavier mount, it delivers half again the firepower.
A large-caliber smoothbore cannon, firing a high-velocity explosive round for piercing thick armor at long range. A specialized autoloader allows for fast followup shots.

A Magellan analog to the fabled Tachyon Lance, but one that lacks any form of miniaturization. This heavy beam emitter could only be made to function by being integrated directly into the hull of the Protectorate's most advanced battlecruiser.
Fires a salvo of small, high-speed rockets that excel at pressuring shields. This strike craft variant carries more ammunition, but requires docking to reload.
Fires a salvo of small, high-speed rockets with next to no payload capacity; the resulting kinetic strike is perfect for stressing shield generators.
Fires a barrage of small, high-speed rockets with next to no payload capacity; the resulting kinetic strike is perfect for stressing shield generators.
A scaled up, extended range Micro Burst Laser rated for ship to ship combat. An unremarkable weapon aside from its simplicity and ruggedness.
Launches a salvo of four anti-fighter missiles with fragmentation warheads.
Launches a salvo of two anti-fighter missiles with fragmentation warheads.
Launches a double salvo of four anti-fighter missiles with fragmentation warheads.
Launches a single anti-fighter missile with a fragmentation warhead.

A launch system for Stormfire mid-range cluster missiles, integrated into the ship's hull. In addition to carrying a staggering ten reloads per tube, it also contains a small autofactory installation to resupply the magazines slowly over time.

A launch system for Balefire heavy fusion missiles, integrated into the ship's hull. In addition to carrying a staggering eight reloads per tube, it also contains a small autofactory installation to resupply the magazines slowly over time.
Projects two devastating pulses of unstable plasma that arc along a ship's hull on impact, disabling weapons and engines.
A tried and tested weapon system, this bay holds several massive unguided warheads that rely on the velocity of the launching craft to reach their target.
A lightweight energy weapon, useful against other fighters and light armor.
Projects a devastating pulse of unstable plasma that arcs along a ship's hull on impact, disabling weapons and engines.
Projects two devastating pulses of unstable plasma that arc along a ship's hull on impact, disabling weapons and engines.
A compact and low-damage EMP missile, mainly useful for distracting point defense and knocking out engines.
A simple machine gun, firing heavy slugs rapidly and with reasonable accuracy.
A simple twin-linked machine gun, firing heavy slugs rapidly and with reasonable accuracy.
A small bay for flux-primed fusion bombs, capable of devastating even hardened targets.

An array of launch racks for heavy, flux-primed fusion bombs, capable of carpeting targets in fire with a single devastating salvo. Because the bombs are externally-primed, they require flux to arm and fire.

A simple discharger for enormous, flux-primed fusion bombs, capable of devastating even hardened targets - provided they can be delivered through point-defenses and shielding. Because the bombs are externally-primed, they require flux to arm and fire.

An ancient, devastating twin-mount heavy autocannon, firing enormous semi-molten bolts in linked salvos. The heavier bolts have excellent penetration, and allow even a single mount to chew through a substantial belt of armor.
While the single-mount Bonecrusher weapon is notoriously inaccurate, this twin turret is pleasantly stable, allowing for much more accurate fire. Turret crews also appreciate the protection afforded by the heavy iridium-composite cast armor.
An enormous, low-velocity artillery piece, firing a massive hellbore-type shell at long range. The detonation is so large it threatens not just the target, but nearby ships as well.
A burst-capable light flak gun, mounted in a twin housing and intended as supplemental point defense.

Fires a barrage of high-speed rockets with limited payload capacity; the resulting kinetic strike is perfect for stressing shield generators, and instead of a conventional warhead, each rocket carries an electron compression charge to destabilize electrical systems as well.

A brute force direct energy microwave emitter adapted from ancient orbital power transfer technology. Although largely ineffective against modern shields, hits against exposed hull produce ruinously disruptive electrical charges.
The Authority Heavy Maser was created to put an end to the unpopular practice of equipping the most powerful ships of the Fleet with imported heavy energy weapons. True to their design philosophy, Magellan engineers simply used their existing technology to upscale their point defense maser emitters as much as physically possible. The end result is equal parts impressive and appalling. While the weapon is devastating against onboard electronics, the less is said about what it does to hapless crew caught in the beam path, the better.
A heavy rotary cannon in an armored housing, firing long bursts of explosive shells to shoot down missiles and fighters. Also highly effective in close combat.
A heavy rotary cannon in a compact mount, firing abbreviated bursts of explosive shells to shoot down missiles and fighters. Also highly effective in close combat.
A high-velocity autocannon, perfect for hammering an enemy shield with salvos of kinetic cluster shells.
A heavy fusion torch, firing a long burst of raw, high-temperature plasma that devours armor and hull plating.
Three standard maser units, linked into a common targeting system and rotated on a common housing. The focused fire of three masers is perfectly adequate to destroy most incoming missiles.

In response to the newly developed Triple Fusion Cannon being integrated into the capital ships of the Blackcollar Regiment, their traditional rivals the Skytiger Guards lobbied for their own version. This weapon, which can match the firepower of the built-in variant for short bursts while being compatible with modular warship mounts, was the result of their efforts.
An oversized beam weapon, closely integrated into the strike craft's power systems.

An advanced spinal-mount magnetic cannon, firing large hypervelocity slugs that stress shield generators and spall into deadly fragments behind armor. Due to the huge recoil and power requirements, this weapon must be integrated into the ship's frame to fire safely.

An advanced magnetic cannon, firing hypervelocity slugs that stress shield generators and spall into deadly fragments behind armor.
Unlike most Magellan weapons, Quench Guns are extremely accurate and fast, and predictably, their crews tend towards the upper end of both the social scale and the career track for gunnery. This is balanced out somewhat by the graphic accounts of what happens if a poorly-maintained solenoid coil should scrape the projectile on the way out of the barrel - typically disassembling the mount explosively, and turning the crew into chunky salsa as the fragments of their weapon spall back into the gunnery station.
A launch bay for fast, light missiles with simple guidance, firing salvoes of three. Each missile is individually weak, but volume of fire and repeated barrages can chew away armor.
A launcher for fast, light missiles with simple guidance, firing salvoes of five. Each missile is individually weak, but volume of fire and repeated barrages can chew away armor.
A launch pod for fast, light missiles with simple guidance, firing salvoes of ten. Each missile is individually weak, but volume of fire and repeated barrages can chew away armor.
A launch pod for fast short-range missiles with simple guidance, firing salvoes of fifteen. Each missile is individually weak, but sheer volume of fire makes them a formidable close-range weapon.
A revolver-breech grenade launcher, firing powerful explosive charges. Capable of sustaining a high rate of fire, for a brief time.
A battery of small rifled cannons, firing a salvo of low-velocity explosive shells at medium range.
Launches a salvo of two anti-fighter missiles with explosive warheads.
A light rotary cannon in an armored housing, firing bursts of explosive shells to shoot down missiles and fighters.
A light rotary cannon in a compact mount, firing abbreviated bursts of explosive shells to shoot down missiles and fighters.

A light rotary autocannon, perfect for hammering an enemy shield with a constant stream of light kinetic shells.
Unlike more typical gatling cannons with fixed barrels, this weapon uses a carousel-type rotating cage to cycle the action, allowing the barrels to recoil individually. Consequently, it's shockingly accurate for a high-velocity autocannon.
A light fusion torch, firing a long burst of raw, high-temperature plasma that devours armor and hull plating.

A simple maser unit, slaved to a point-defense microcomputer and mounted to a high-torque turret. While useless against shields or armor, the bursts of intense microwaves destroy incoming missiles at a surprisingly low flux cost.
An unremarkable lightweight burst laser unit, commonly mounted on civilian ships as a defensive weapon in Magellan space.

A light, accurate autocannon, perfect for straining an enemy shield with a burst of light kinetic shells.
While it has little else to recommend it, this weapon is popular for the simple fact that it allows smaller and weaker ships to contribute to a fight from the backline; many Magellan commanders also find that the weapon is useful in bulk on larger ships with abundant small mounts.
A rack of high-speed dumbfire torpedoes, largely unremarkable except for their blistering terminal speed.
A high-speed dumbfire torpedo, largely unremarkable except for its blistering terminal speed.
A simple magnetic cannon, firing unusually large, dense slugs.
A battery of simple magnetic cannon, firing a salvo of unusually large, dense slugs.

Fires a pair of heavy two-stage bombardment missiles with enormous fragmentation warheads, each scattering a huge payload of shrapnel over a wide area. Effective against most armor, and devastating to smaller targets.

Fires a salvo of four heavy, clumsy long-range missiles with large fragmentation warheads, each scattering a generous payload of shrapnel over a wide area. Ineffective against heavy armor, but devastating to smaller targets.
A light flak projector, mounted in an armored housing and intended as supplemental point defense.
A light flak projector, mounted in an armored housing and intended as supplemental point defense.

Essentially a self guided drone equipped with a miniature weaponized Alcubierre drive, this unconventional anti-ship missile can achieve a brief burst of tremendous acceleration prior to a kinetic kill. As the payload is based on simplistic first generation FTL technology, the missiles can be assembled on site, although their bulk severely limits munitions storage.

So, you take three smaller lasers, and you aim them at the same spot. It's easier to cool, and still great at melting stuff."

"Only way something that small can throw a slug that fast is the integrated mount; if you try to put that on a modular fitting, even odds it'll rip itself loose in a couple of shots."
A simple low-powered laser for illuminating a target ship, scarcely worth mentioning in the same breath as actual weaponry.
A launch bay for Strikefire MRMs, holding two rounds in a compact rack.
A launch tube for Strikefire MRMs, holding six rounds in a compact internal magazine.

"There's violent, there's crude, and there's heaps of fun, and sometimes in this business, you get the glorious privilege to fire and to write about weapons that are all three at once, with whipped cream and a big red cherry on top."

text1: A jewel-like ocean world, home to the ruling aristocracy of the Magellan Protectorate. Enormous, semi-mobile platforms support glorious, glittering arcology-estates, each more delicate and gaudy than the last as they drift lazily over the brilliant waters. Heavily-armed ocean platforms swirl around the surface as well, constantly tracking any nearby orbital ships deemed to be threats by a planet-wide network of sensors.
text3: A shining blue marble around Magella's orange vastness, Annore is a world at once beautiful and forbidding; the spires of her ethereal ocean estates gleam bright, almost obscuring the long, questing muzzles of STO rocket-gun batteries that interrogate the heavens for outsider mischief. The good life is on display here; a rich, aristocratic tradition of plenty and sophistication by Sector standards. Mute personal servants and whimsical automatons scamper after every citizen's whim and fancy, and high technology invisibly secures a vast array of privileges for those honored to call themselves Citizens of Annore. The Protectorate's ruling class forms yet another tier of rarefied aristocratic power and status, above even the citizenry of this hermetic paradise.

text1: A small station by the standards of the wealth and privilege enjoyed by Annore's inhabitants. Annore Orbital is a surprisingly busy commercial starport, importing and exporting a huge volume of goods for the benefit of the planet below. Automated refining and manufacturing take place here, tastefully separated from Annore itself.
text3: A combination of commercial starport and vast government structure, Annore Orbital is home to the twice-yearly Convocation, in which the leading families of Annore gather to divide the material spoils of a brutally pointed social pyramid. The bacchanal atmosphere suffuses the station the rest of the year round; a 'trip upstairs', as the locals call it, is almost always an occasion for debauchery and dissipated excess.

text1: Parched dry and crowded with semi-buried cities, Jeshad is a harsh planet, scoured by dust storms that can imperil the most hardened landing craft. The bulk of the Magellan population lives here, crammed into arcologies that ring the narrow livable belts around the poles where temperatures are bearable most of the day.
text3: A desperately dry, overpopulated world, Jeshad is the manpower reserve that keeps the Magellan state afloat; recruits for the Fleet and the Protector's Army are levied on Jeshad, offering pay and benefits that seem munificent to the inhabitants of the crowded, parched hive-cities that ring the cooler poles. Nomadic raiders travel the great equatorial deserts, raiding outlying settlements and skirmishing with one another using everything from primitive chemical firearms to surprisingly modern energy weaponry. Each clan hews to no law but their own in the fleets of armored rovers they call home, while their punctiliousness in matters of honor and cut-throat competition for resources have made them both highly fractious and highly skilled. Attempts to recruit the desert nomads for the Fleet have been a mixed success; some of the greatest Magellan heroes and worst mutineers have hailed from the deep deserts of Jeshad.

text1: A sight to behold, and the dominant orbital body in the night skies of both Annore and Jeshad, the gas giant Magella orbits close around Khamn, glowing like a second sun from the reflected light.
text3: Majestic and hazardous in equal measure, Magella is intensively mined for volatiles by a small flotilla of independent gas harvesters; every now and then, one of the ill-maintained, scrappy craft will plummet into the roiling cloudbanks in a shower of light and screaming metal.

text1: Barren, but with ideal conditions for antimatter fuel production, Pariya is entirely administered by the Tichel Mercantile Concern. The surface hosts a sizable outpost around the primary fuel production plant and volatiles storage facility, and is well defended by a network of heavy gun batteries.
text3:
Pariya's spaceport is constantly crowded by a flock of small, ramshackle mining craft from nearby Magella, who are forced to dock here and sell their meager cache of volatiles to the sole authorized buyer in the Protectorate. Yet this inter-system trade is a mere sideshow to the steady imports arriving from further afield, a trade likewise dominated entirely by the Tichel Mercantile Concern. 
The rugged, spartan fuel production bases and outlying security outposts on Pariya's surface look and feel far more like a military outpost than a commercial endeavor; armed guards in the gray and gold uniform of the Tichel Yellowtails are everywhere, ready to harassing workers and independent spacers alike with obnoxious eagerness.

text1: A temperate desert world verging on airless, Turan is home to both substantial heavy industry and a small agricultural colony, populated chiefly by Magellan dissidents and exiles.
text3: Unlike the vastly less hospitable colony of Valca, the rift valleys and deeper craters of Turan are shirt-sleeve habitable by human beings, albeit with breath masks for anything longer than a quick hike. A competitive industrial sector and hardy farming domes ensure that the planetary government is merely subservient to the Magellan governing structure that dominates local space; interference in local affairs is rare, and the smarter locals work to keep it that way.

text1: A small customs port, mainly useful for sustaining the defense platform that protects Turan from invasion.
text3: This little port is vastly overshadowed by Meetpoint Turan, and spacers avoid docking here if possible in favor of the larger, more favorable station in higher orbit.

text1: Icy, foreboding, but nevertheless rich in volatiles, the Valca colony is technically independent of Magellan control, and serves a secondary purpose as a dumping ground for undesirables.
text3: A frozen world with rich deposits of volatiles, Valca was colonized to supply the Fleet's new fuel production facilities and just as quickly became a hotbed of dissent; the solution was to declare the planet nominally independent, and lock the new government into a highly favorable contract for volatile supply. Port controls and the station in orbit keep trouble that brews on the surface contained there, while poverty and the harsh surface conditions impose their own kind of order on any exiles looking to return home at the head of a revolution.

text1: Orbiting the nominally independent world of Valca, while remaining under the control of the Magellan Protectorate, Valca Bastion is a substantial military outpost designed mainly to contain the restive populations of Valca and Turan, as well as to ensure the volatile supply to Pariya's new fuel facility proceeds without interruption.
text3: A veritable sword of Damocles hanging over the planet below, Valca Bastion stands ready to intervene at a moment's notice if the supply of volatiles to Pariya should ever come under serious threat. The garrison here is well-paid, but has relatively few options for off-shift activities; predictably, there's a thriving culture of heavy binge-drinking and petty violence in addition to the usual run of officially-sanctioned leisure.

text1: An obsolete and somewhat decrepit starport, repurposed as the headquarters of the local free-mercantile association.
text3: While Magellan space could hardly be called a commercial paradise, what trade in the local volume of space that can be called independent is headquartered here - a ramshackle, swapmeet-freeport where every ship's deck is a law unto itself and no sensible spacer gets between two crews with a grudge. Captains who dock here are notorious for accepting little to no restraint on their trade, their movements, and their much-touted customary rights to refuse inspection, declaration, or taxation on their cargoes. Many are little better than pirates, given half an opportunity and a halfway-plausible letter of marque or 'militia' licensure, and much of the trade that goes through here is as much about goods fenced as goods exchanged.

text1: Desolate and unremarkable, the local pirates and criminal gangs have established a small swapmeet port on this otherwise useless world.
text3: Almost nothing about this planetesimal is in any way remarkable; it's purely interesting due to the dug-in pirate base that sits under thick layers of compacted regolith and metalloceramic armor. In spite, rather than because, of this excessive dedication to protection, the locals are more paranoid that usual; fears of a strike on unprotected domes by the Fleet or a local militia are supplanted or augmented by fears of internal power struggles to control a desirable base of operations.

text1: A desolate, frozen rock with little to offer, Spera was a Fleet-run penal colony reserved for the most dangerous political criminals. When Port Obilo mutinied, the Spera prison camp fell into revolt, and the surface facility was abandoned.
text3: The base here was mainly constructed of pressurized fabric anti-rad domes, supported by flexible aluminum girders; little of either survived the revolt. A few twisted scraps of metal and desiccated plasticloth are all that remain near the sputtering landing beacon.

text1: A massive ancient sporeship hull from the original exile fleet, heavily fortified and operating as the sovereign military stronghold and staging base of the Blackcollar Regiment.
text3: The ancient sporeship hulk known as Crucible Base has been retrofitted by the Blackcollar Regiment into a formidable orbital fortress and logistics hub. While part of the vessel remains consecrated as a solemn memorial tomb to generations of fallen soldiers, its gargantuan interior bays now house active munitions foundries, heavy staging docks, and elite shock-trooper barracks. Spacers and licensed privateers permitted to dock here will find a well-supplied arms market offering upgraded warships, experimental weaponry, and combat LPCs rarely sanctioned for the civilian fleet.

text1: A fortified haven nestled deep within the electromagnetic turbulence of the Rose Nebula, serving as the hidden redoubt, command post, and shipyard of the Leveller underground.
text3: Once thought to be an abandoned casualty of the first Leveller Uprising, Rosebriar Station has been secretly revitalized and expanded into the Leveller movement's primary sanctuary and operations hub. Hidden beneath the dense plasma sheets and dust storms of the Rose Nebula, the station houses weapon modification workshops, clandestine printing suites, and refit berths for turncoat warships. While the central memorial hall preserves the sacred memories of past revolutions, the station's concourses hum with revolutionary fervor, barter trade, and insurgent logistics.

text1: A storm-scoured toxic world housing the industrial heart of the Herd, where outlaw refineries and illicit ship-breaking yards operate under caustic skies.
text3: Acrid is a harsh, poison-soaked world whose dense acidic atmosphere and violent chemical storms would deter any lawful enterprise. For the Herd, however, its deep volcanic craters and abundant heavy ores provide the ideal secluded cradle for illicit manufacturing. Massive geothermal smelters and scrap foundries churn day and night, producing crude armor plating, high-explosive ordnance, and makeshift strikecraft to fuel the raider fleets that terrorize the surrounding systems.

text1: An intensely irradiated desert world whose subterranean complexes and canyon redoubts serve as the primary fleet bastion and command lair of the Herd.
text3: Blistered by relentless solar radiation and geothermal heat, the surface of Scorched is lethal to unprotected life. Beneath its jagged obsidian canyons and basalt shields, however, lies an extensive warren of blast-hardened subterranean bunkers and drydocks. From this fortified lair, Herd warlords coordinate deep-space ambushes and maintain heavily modified combat vessels, protected from orbital surveillance by thick layers of lead-rich regolith.

text1: A frozen, airless rock at the edge of Dunerunner's Rest, functioning as a forward listening post, missile depot, and raider staging facility for the Herd.
text3: Cold, desolate, and heavily pitted by ancient meteor impacts, Desolation sits in silent vigil on the outer rim of Dunerunner's Rest. Its subsurface silos hold stockpiles of volatile munitions, auxiliary fuel reserves, and automated defense batteries. Fast attack flotillas and scavenger wolfpacks frequently stage from Desolation's subterranean docking bays before launching lightning raids into the Core Systems.

text1: A dusty world of cattle ranching and extreme corruption, Calicheman is an anarchic freeport more or less by accident. Few ships touch down here with legitimate business, but all are welcome.
text3: Too poor and too marginal to justify the returns, Calicheman has never been worth bringing under any kind of central control; neither the Magellan Protectorate nor any organized independent government or corporation can profitably control the planet, and so far none have been unwise enough to try. This suits the prickly locals just fine; few enough of them care about the wider galaxy unless it has something to trade for hides and jerky.

text1: Part scrapyard, part fortress, this half-destroyed hulk was formerly a mining base in the inner system, but has been refitted as a de facto headquarters for several of the local salvage organizations and crime syndicates.
text3: Already marginal when the easy pickings of the local belt were exhausted, this once-promising mining facility in the inner system fell to a revolt and was swiftly abandoned to its fate by a Fleet that had no need of the meager trickle of resources it was by then bringing in. In a brief fit of high-minded moralism, it was renamed Ghammol Station after an outback town razed by the Blackcollars during the first Leveller Uprising.

text1: Once an outer system early-warning post, Port Obilo fell to mutiny during a series of upheavals on Jeshad, coordinated with a general rebellion in the Fleet's patrol forces. Now, it's the locus of most illegal activity in the system; whatever your darkest desire, it can be found here.
text3: Every society has an underbelly, and Magellan society has more than most; Port Obilo's ramshackle concourses house everything from the most incorrigible career criminals to naive Leveller revolutionaries. All the inhabitants really have in common is their inability to make lives for themselves on either Annore or Jeshad, and fights are common, but they're in agreement on one point; the station batteries and minefields that keep the Fleet at bay must be maintained, whatever the cost.

text1:
A primitive distress beacon, ejected automatically from an early generation colonization vessel. Contains a solid-state power system which enables theoretical operation and station-keeping half-life with an upwards range in the tens of thousands of cycles.
The astute starship captain will likely find items of value nearby.

An automated supply barge that accompanied the arrival of the exiled Magellan Fleet in what would become the Persean Sector.
Hundreds of these automated logistics barges were deployed to support the colony ships, and in emergencies, attempted to rescue colonists whose ships failed during the long journey. This apparently unresponsive hulk has been ravaged by centuries of exposure to charged particles and high velocity impacts from interstellar dust.

One of the legendary Alcubierre drive colony ships that brought the Magellan exiles to this region of space, a rugged and terrifyingly primitive vessel - even by the fallen standards of the post-Collapse Persean Sector.
Triply- or quadruply-redundant in all major systems and built to withstand centuries of continuous flight, these colony ships contain a rudimentary autoforge capacity to manufacture a suite of smaller vessels and the supplies required to perform its ongoing mission. This specimen is burned and battered by its centuries of plodding travel, a drifting, forgotten hulk.

One of the legendary motherships that led the exiled Magellan Fleet to this region of space, a huge and massively redundant slab of armor and autofactories, capable of single-handedly traversing vast distances with its early, unreliable hyperdrive.
Triply- or quadruply-redundant in all major systems and built to withstand centuries of continuous flight, these motherships contained an impressive autoforge capacity to facilitate colonization efforts. This specimen is burned and battered by its centuries of plodding travel, a drifting, forgotten hulk.

A militaristic, closed society, founded before the recorded settlement of the Persean Sector by an STL fleet of refugees from a rebellion against the Domain of Man. Harried by Domain drone weaponry and trapped in their aging early-model sporeships, the Fleet that would become the Magellan Protectorate developed a rigid and brutal caste system that persists to the present, as well as a rough-edged, and inward-turned, culture.
Deeply suspicious of outsiders and equipped with a unique technological heritage based on long-obsolescent Domain hardware, the Magellan Protectorate has held its own against the rest of the Sector's inhabitants... so far.

Lusty, violent, and above all radioactive; the pirate gang known as The Herd hails from the marginal steppe world of Calicheman, and has plagued Magellan space since regular commercial travel between the systems of the cluster became practical. While unpredictable and terrifying to civilian traders, their ramshackle and poorly-maintained vessels are no match for the mighty battle-line of the Magellan Fleet.

A radical egalitarian movement within Magellan society, the Levellers are a small but vocal minority party, often banned outright under more repressive High Protectors, with an energetic armed wing; ever-ready to strike against the forces of the state - often with little to no regard for innocent bystanders. No act is too extreme in pursuit of their ideal society, and nothing less than complete abolition of social class and unequal treatment before the law will satisfy the Levellers.

The premier shock infantry and heavy assault marine regiment of the Magellan Protectorate. Operating from fortified redoubts like Crucible Base, the Blackcollars field hardened warships with heavy ballistic batteries and modular fighter flight bays, spearheading offensive operations with ruthless discipline.

The armed security, logistical, and privateering arm of the Tichel Mercantile Concern. Administering fuel production at Pariya, the Yellowtails operate fast blockade runners, heavy freighters, and escort craft to monopolize local trade across the Protectorate.

The elite royal vanguard and high-readiness aerospace detachment tasked with the defense of Annore and high-value orbital infrastructure. Known for piloting rapid interceptors and agile carrier strike wings, the Skytigers maintain strict vigilance over the core worlds.

Direct descendants of the original sleeper crews and voidfarers who navigated the Alcubierre-drive exile fleet from the Domain. They maintain ancient vessel hulls, relic survey technology, and deep void-faring traditions from their stronghold on Turan.
Independent asteroid miners, wreck-breakers, and civilian salvage crews operating across the Khamn cluster and surrounding debris fields, trading salvage and ore with any port willing to pay.

Centuries-old automated defense drones and emergency AI cores still guarding the drifting hulks of the original Magellan exile fleet. Programmed to defend their ancestral wrecks against all intruders, they operate with cold, unwavering precision.

Free merchants, independent spacers, and guild captains operating outside the direct command of the High Protector, headquartered at Meetpoint Turan where the Guild of Free Traders ensures open commerce.
A tough, well-protected attack corvette, armed with a powerful turret and anti-armor missiles, refitted by the Blackcollars as a gunship. Highly effective against unshielded or vulnerable targets.
A heavily armored bomber, deploying twin missile bays, refitted by the Blackcollars as a standoff bomber. Effective at harrying enemy vessels from a safe distance.
A lightly armored support fighter wielding a heavy nose-mounted Bonethrower Cannon.

A heavily modified Edger-class Carrier. Modifications include the replacement of a flight deck with a large hardpoint, the removal of the shuttle bay in favor of an immense missile array, and an all-ballitic loadout for maximum firepower. Furthermore, a unique set of Lochaber fighters armed with cutting lasers and defensive mines accompany this vessel.
Despite Tai Cor-Lan's first creations appealing to the Herdmaster greatly, their slow pace began stressing the relationship. Endeavoring to keep his connection to the Herd at arm's length, the former Blackcollar engineer formed a group and set out with his latest creations to pillage surrounding space in an effort to appease the demanding Herdmaster. While successful, his actions were severe enough to earn the ire of the Fleet's professional military arm, and has been on the run since.
An armored support fighter, deploying a cutting laser and defensive mines. Modified to keep frontal threats at bay through massed laser fire and a thick screen of flak pods.

A heavily modified Jitte-class Fighter. Modifications include extra thrusters, an upgraded main cannon, underslung autoguns, and a set of powerful fuel injectors. A wing of similarly-altered mod-fighters also accompany this unique vessel.
Though it appears ungainly and haphazard from a distance, the well-designed machine spaces and sleek lines of the ship say otherwise. Tai Cor-Lan was a promising engineering officer recruited from the dunes of Jeshad into the Blackcollar Regiment before becoming disillusioned and falling in with the Herd. He is also known to be allied, or at least do business, with the Dunerunners and their associates. This combined with the authority of the Herd and his technical acumen allowed him to create a number of surprisingly powerful designs, this ranking among them.
Powerful, fast and well shielded, a heavy fighter that can survive close combat around cruisers and capitals. Heavily modified by the Marauders for a powerful first strike.

A heavily modified Bastardsword-class Corvette. Modifications include extra armor, an altered lance, and an enormous underslung cannon. A wing of similarly-altered mod-corvettes also accompany this unique vessel.
Though it appears ungainly and haphazard from a distance, the well-designed machine spaces and sleek lines of the ship say otherwise. Tai Cor-Lan was a promising engineering officer recruited from the dunes of Jeshad into the Blackcollar Regiment before becoming disillusioned and falling in with the Herd. He is also known to be allied, or at least do business, with the Dunerunners and their associates. This combined with the authority of the Herd and his technical acumen allowed him to create a number of surprisingly powerful designs, this ranking among them.
A tough, well-protected attack corvette, armed with a deadly shotgun and armor-stripping missiles. Heavily modified by the Marauders for endurance and attrition.

A tough, well-protected corvette, reconditioned and modified to serve the Leveller cause. These modifications allow the corvette to operate independently (albeit briefly) and include additional software to coordinate a wing of swarmfighter drones.
Alterations include a modularized flux system, improved maneuverability, upgraded weapons systems, and the addition of a command system coordinate a drone wing. However, due to the complexity and widespread series of upgrades, these can no longer be produced as standard fighter LPCs. In spite of this, the large and open design of the Bastardsword Corvette lends itself well to modification, something the Levellers have no shortage of experience with.

An extraordinary ship created in secret for a client affiliated with the Levellers. Many of the systems have been extensively modified by SNRI Labs and the Levellers to produce a unique vessel capable of extreme speed and maneuverability.
Despite the secrecy involved in her creation, a number of databanks hold information on her creation, possibly due to the crew's unfamiliarity with proprietary DME systems. The entries record that SNRI scientists and engineers were excited to have received a Magellan Capella, especially as it had Blackcollar upgrades - one of the Protectorate's most advanced vessels - for modification through a business associate. On seeing the ship, the project lead was immediately struck with a vision and began the conversion process. After some tripping over the obscurities of Magellan technology, the program would eventually manage to retrofit a Sigma Reaction Furnce into the frame, install an advanced shield generator, and replace some now-unused exterior shield nodes with a suite of multi-beamer PD nodes and missile silos. However, the intensive modifications to the power and flux systems mean that further tweaks can cause undue stress to the vessel, though this was considered an acceptable drawback in exchange for improved baseline performance.
While the project lead expressed dissatisfaction at being unable to install the MIRAGE System due to space restrictions, the Levellers who received the ship were thoroughly impressed. More familiar with Magellan technology, they proceeded to overhaul the engine assembly and targeting systems while also integrating a devastating Magnetic Hypergun into the frame. The result is an incredible, one-of-a-kind ship capable of acrobatic feats that would put most frigates to shame, and armed with enough firepower to subdue cruisers under a skilled hand.

A highly modified Talley-class Merchanter. Modifications include further firepower in addition to elaborate systems upgrades which present a formidable opponent in battle.
Despite the amount of effort and materials needed to convert a single example, these ships are not entirely unique - a number are known to exist, almost entirely in the hands of a mercenary group by the name of 'The Dunerunners'. Hiding behind the innocent title of Merchanter, this mod-ship is known to contain high-end parts smuggled in from nearly every major manufacturer in the Sector, and the payoffs are evident. Armor reinforcement designs from Chicomoztoc, engine parts from Kazeron, subsystems optimizations from Culann, cargo bay shielding from Kanta's Den, an extendable salvage gantry from Agreus, and many others. A pair of flexible sponsons have been added to the port and starboard cargo bays for additional firepower, and an auxiliary space has been repurposed to house a combat support drone. Furthermore, the design maintains the current logistical profile with incredibly few downsides. A large smuggling ring would be needed to obtain new parts for just one of these ships, let alone a small fleet of them.

A highly modified Kant-class Scoutship. Modifications include further firepower in addition to elaborate systems upgrades which present a formidable opponent in battle.
Despite the amount of effort and materials needed to convert a single example, these ships are not entirely unique - a number are known to exist, almost entirely in the hands of a mercenary group by the name of 'The Dunerunners'. This mod-ship appears to have originally been a Blackcollar-grade Kant-class Scoutship, highly upgraded with a few notable specializations. Already atmospheric-capable, the pre-existing ground support package was upgraded and the sensors package replaced with specialized surveying equipment. An additional set of missile sponsons and a composite hardpoint round out the series of upgrades while maintaining the current logistical profile. A high-profile connection with unscrupulous morals within the Fleet would be needed to acquire just one Blackcollar Kant, let alone a small fleet of them.
An advanced point-defense drone, highly modified from its base spec for a more support-oriented role.

A relic of the Fleet's past, lacking the refinement and flexibility of more recent examples. However, this hulk retains a set of ancient lances that, despite being outmoded by modern weapons design, remain capable of punishing even the most heavily armored targets.
A truly antediluvian vessel, the manufacturing dates on this ship put its creation before the Domain of Man even set foot in the Persean Sector. It bears all the hallmarks of the early epoch of ship design - bulky, non-modular energy weapons, a lack of shields, and a vulnerability to strike weapons. While the databanks have been thoroughly scrubbed or corrupted by radiation, certain assumptions can be made by examining the nature of the ship. The lack of shields, nor even the provisions for one, point to her sheer age. A significant amount of armor had been trimmed at some point after she was launched, crudely cut off in some areas. Her bulky energy turrets are permanently mounted and share no parts with any known weapons platform, and related systems are especially patchy and unreliable even after a full reset.
All these point to this vessel being an experimental platform to test technological and military theory. When she was lost, she took with her all that had been learned, leaving the Fleet with an empty hand and little to show for it. While contemporary advancements have already eclipsed anything that could have been learned from the deployment of this ship, her unique design and powerful weaponry still pose a very real threat in the modern battlespace.
Supercharges one of the Swarmfighter drones with a brief energy transfer. The drone tracks a nearby target like a missile, dealing large area damage on impact.
text3: Supercharges one of the Swarmfighter drones and sends it after a target. The drone deals 500 High Explosive damage on impact, and an additional 500 Fragmentation damage on hits to armor or hull, and charging it generates 500 flux.

text1:
A compact turret housing quadruple barrels firing heavy Boneshaker bolts. An advanced double-loader system allows this weapon to unleash a remarkably large salvo, though accuracy suffers.
This weapon earned the nickname 'Valca Piano' during one spectacular incident in the Karic system while suppressing the notoriously dissident population.

A quad mounting of the Light Flenser CIWS system, capable of putting up a constant wall of ordnance. However, the loading systems struggle to keep up with the blistering rate of ammunition expenditure.
The explosive shells, though small, have an outsized effect against even heavy armor through sheer volume of fire. Many a Herd captain has fallen afoul of the expectation that they would be safe from a mere point-defense weapon.

A lance weapon developed in antiquity before shield technology became widespread. Devastating against exposed hull, with respectable performance against heavy armor.
A legendary weapon from the Protectorate's past, responsible for the destruction of innumerable war drones as the Fleet escaped the grip of the Domain. While performance against shields leaves much to be desired, its brute-force approach to stripping armor and hull wins it much favor in certain circles.
A launch tube for high-speed dumbfire torpedoes, largely unremarkable except for their blistering terminal speed.
A compact and terrifying fragmentation shotgun integrated into the corvette's systems for improved fire rate and range.
A revolver-breech grenade launcher firing powerful explosive charges, closely integrated into the corvette's systems.
Launches a salvo of two fast, light missiles with simple guidance.

An internal magazine of Balefire heavy fusion missiles. While not as powerful as dedicated anti-armor missiles, the Balefire is more effective against shields. Disposable canisters and an external arm allow aiming and firing at any angle.
An underwing launcher for fast, light missiles with simple guidance, firing salvos of four.
A modified and lightened Bonecrusher integrated into the frame of the fighter, the Bonethrower boasts excellent engagement range at cost of sustained rate of fire.
A light, accurate autocannon, integrated into the Centauro's systems to provide increased range.
Launches a single anti-fighter missile with a fragmentation warhead.
A rack of Stunfire rocket grenades, fired in pairs.
A heavy twin-linked Diffusion Gun, closely integrated into the corvette's power systems. While capable of a powerful alpha strike, the corvette's systems can't keep up with the demands for long.

text1: The product of a rich Annorian noble with too much money to spend, it was originally created as a pleasure craft to explore the depths below and the space above. A tough, well-protected bomber, armed with a point-defense cannon and bomb bay, refitted by The Herd with extra thrusters and a heavily modified fusion bomb. Devastating against all targets.

A Ballistic Accelerator has also been installed to further increase firepower. A wing of modified Bastardsword-class Corvettes also accompany this unique vessel.

text1: A highly modified targeting drone, gutted and redesigned for fire support. A shield emitter has been installed, the PD Maser upgraded, and the targeting equipment stripped out and replaced with a light autocannon and light missile system in addition to much-needed improvements to armor and durability.

A highly maneuverable strikecraft with an extremely flexible loadout. A wide shield and easy recovery make up for it's lack of durability, while further modifications allow the heavy fighter to operate independently (albeit briefly) and include additional software to coordinate a wide variety of fighter wings.
The Bounder has its origins as Rounder-class Heavy Fighters, liberated by ambitious miners and salvors from the ship graveyard that surrounds Ghammol Station. They first found use as utility vessels, mounting lasers and blasting charges to expose the easy pickings of the belt and break open hulks. As the facility fell to revolt, Bounders were quickly repurposed as strike craft to defend the newly-independent station, and were found to be quite effective. The former miners saw an opportunity to create a potent strike weapon, so they developed a process to refit, upgrade, and modularize the ancient vessels using parts scavenged from the graveyard. While unable to directly produce upgraded examples, some inventive salvors sliced the autofactory out of a Mallory in order to produce less-degraded Rounders for conversion. Capable of mounting an obscene amount of ordnance under the right conditions, it caught the attention of mercenaries passing through the system and has since proliferated to the Core.
